operativeSourceText:
“Consolidated
Interest Expense” means, with respect to any Person for any period, without duplication, the sum of:
(a) cash
interest expense (including that attributable to Capitalized Lease Obligations), net of cash interest income, with respect to Indebtedness of such Person and its Subsidiaries for such period, other than
Non-Recourse Indebtedness, including commissions, discounts and other fees and charges owed with respect to letters of credit and bankers’ acceptance financing and net cash costs under hedging agreements
(other than in connection with the early termination thereof); plus
(b)
non-cash interest expense resulting solely from (i) the amortization of original issue discount from the issuance of Indebtedness of such Person and its Subsidiaries at less than par (excluding any
Indebtedness borrowed under the Facilities in connection with the Transactions and any Non-Recourse Indebtedness), plus
(ii) pay-in-kind interest expense of such Person and its Subsidiaries payable pursuant to the terms of the agreements governing Indebtedness for borrowed money;

excluding, in each case:

(i) amortization of deferred financing costs, debt issuance costs, commissions, fees and expenses and any other amounts of non-cash interest other than referred to in clauses (b)(i) and (b)(ii) above (including as a result of the effects of acquisition method accounting or pushdown accounting),

(ii) interest expense attributable to the movement of the
mark-to-market valuation of obligations under Hedging Obligations and any other derivative instruments, including pursuant to FASB Accounting Standards Codification
Topic 815, Derivatives and Hedging,
(iii) costs associated with incurring or terminating Hedging Obligations and
cash costs associated with breakage in respect of hedging agreements for interest rates,
(iv) commissions, discounts,
yield, make-whole premium and other fees and charges (including any interest expense) incurred in connection with any Non-Recourse Indebtedness,

(v) “additional interest” owing pursuant to a registration rights agreement with respect to any securities,

(vi) any payments with respect to make-whole premiums or other breakage costs of any Indebtedness, including any Indebtedness
issued in connection with the Transactions,

20

(vii) penalties and interest relating to taxes,

(viii) accretion or accrual of discounted liabilities not constituting Indebtedness,

(ix) [reserved],

(x) any expense resulting from the discounting of Indebtedness in connection with the application of recapitalization or
purchase accounting,
(xi) any interest expense attributable to the exercise of appraisal rights and the settlement of any
claims or actions (whether actual, contingent or potential) with respect thereto in connection with the Transactions, any acquisition or Investment and

(xii) annual agency fees paid to any administrative agents and collateral agents with respect to any secured or unsecured
loans, debt facilities, debentures, bonds, commercial paper facilities or other forms of Indebtedness (including any security or collateral trust arrangements related thereto), including the Facilities and the Super-Priority Revolving Credit
Agreement.
For purposes of this definition, interest on a Capitalized Lease Obligation will be deemed to accrue at an interest rate reasonably determined
by such Person to be the rate of interest implicit in such Capitalized Lease Obligation in accordance with GAAP.

sufficiencyReasons: Top-level additive structure (cash component (a) net of cash interest income, plus non-cash OID amortization (b)(i), plus PIK interest (b)(ii)) is faithfully represented.

The twelve numbered 'excluding' carve-outs (i)-(xii) (e.g. deferred financing cost amortization, mark-to-market hedging movements, make-whole/breakage costs, tax penalties/interest, Non-Recourse Indebtedness fees, agency fees, etc.) are categorical scope-narrowing clarifications of what is NOT included within components (a)/(b) in the first place, rather than independently quantifiable subtracted amounts - they are captured descriptively in the metric naming/citation/excerpt but are not separately decomposed as arithmetic nodes, since no IR primitive cleanly expresses a non-quantified categorical scope exclusion distinct from SUBTRACT of a computed amount.

Dependent defined terms (Non-Recourse Indebtedness, Capitalized Lease Obligations, Indebtedness, Hedging Obligations, Transactions, Facilities, Super-Priority Revolving Credit Agreement) were not independently resolved/fetched; their scope is assumed from ordinary usage embedded in the metric descriptions above.

findings.sourceCitation: §1.01 (Consolidated Interest Expense), 'excluding, in each case' clauses (i)-(xii)
findings.proposedIrEvidence: calculationExpression = ADD( SUBTRACT(cash interest expense, cash interest income) [clause (a)], ADD(OID amortization, PIK interest) [clause (b)(i)+(b)(ii)] ) - no EXCLUDE node, no representation of any of the twelve 'excluding, in each case' clauses, and no metadata anywhere in the definition entry disclosing that these clauses were omitted (contrast with the adjacent 'Consolidated Maintenance EBITDA' entry, which explicitly discloses its own gap).
findings.verifierReasoning: The source definition is structurally 'sum of (a) plus (b), excluding, in each case: (i)-(xii)' - the twelve exclusion clauses are an independently operative, textually explicit modifier that applies to the entire sum, not incidental commentary. They carve out substantively significant items (e.g., mark-to-market movements on hedging obligations, tax penalties and interest, annual agency fees to administrative/collateral agents, make-whole/breakage payments, appraisal-rights-related interest, recapitalization/purchase-accounting discounting effects, registration-rights 'additional interest') that would otherwise plausibly be swept into a literal reading of clauses (a) and (b) (e.g., 'other fees and charges' in (a), or 'any other amounts of non-cash interest' analogous to (b)). The proposed IR's calculationExpression represents Consolidated Interest Expense as simply (a) + (b) with no exclusion logic anywhere, and the definition's sufficiency tag of 'PARTIAL' is not accompanied by any explanation identifying this specific gap (unlike the neighboring Consolidated Maintenance EBITDA entry, which explicitly and transparently describes what is missing and why). A downstream user of this IR could reasonably compute a materially inflated Consolidated Interest Expense (e.g., by including annual agency fees, tax penalties, or mark-to-market hedging losses) relative to what the contract actually requires, which would directly affect any covenant (e.g., interest coverage ratio, debt incurrence test) that depends on this defined term. This is exactly the kind of omission the deterministic signals flagged: 13 enumerated units compiled into 0 rules, and 6 conditional/exception markers reflected as zero conditions in the IR - both point to the same real gap, the wholesale absence of the exclusion clauses from the compiled calculation.
